title: GraphRAG and LazyGraphRAG
summary: GraphRAG builds an entity graph and community summaries so a system can answer whole-corpus questions that top-k chunks cannot. LazyGraphRAG defers the expensive model work to query time.
useIf: Users ask global or thematic questions such as 'what are the main themes across these reports?', or answers require linking entities across documents.
avoidIf: Questions are single-fact lookups, the corpus changes quickly, or per-user permissions apply inside community summaries.

explain.md: Top-k vector RAG retrieves the chunks nearest a question. A question like 'what are the recurring root causes across all incident reports?' has no single nearest chunk. **GraphRAG** indexes differently. An LLM extracts entities, relationships and claims from text units and builds a graph. The graph is clustered hierarchically with the Leiden algorithm, and the LLM writes a **summary for every community**. Global queries run over those summaries. The query modes are Global, Local, DRIFT and Basic, and the indexing methods are `standard` (the LLM does all reasoning, the default) and `FastGraphRAG` (classic NLP replaces some LLM steps) [[r40]] [[r16]].

explain.title: GraphRAG indexing and global query
explain.alt: Documents become text units, entities and relationships form a graph, communities are summarised, and a global query is answered from the community summaries.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  D[Documents] --> T[Text units]
  T --> E[Entities and relations]
  E --> G[Graph]
  G --> C[Leiden communities]
  C --> S[Community summaries]
  Q[Global question] --> M[Map over summaries]
  S --> M
  M --> A[Answer]

explain.md: **The cost problem and LazyGraphRAG.** Full GraphRAG spends many LLM calls at indexing time. Microsoft Research's LazyGraphRAG (blog dated 2024-11-25) reports indexing cost identical to vector RAG and 0.1% of full GraphRAG, answer quality comparable to GraphRAG Global Search on global queries at more than 700 times lower query cost, and, at 4% of the query cost of GraphRAG global search, better results than all compared methods. It exposes one cost-quality dial, the relevance test budget. These are the vendor's own benchmark numbers. An editor's note dated 2025-06-06 says it is integrated into Microsoft Discovery and Azure Local in public preview [[r17]].

**Sibling idea.** RAPTOR clusters and summarises chunks recursively into a tree, so retrieval can pull from several abstraction levels. Paired with GPT-4 it raised the best QuALITY result by 20% absolute, and indexing LLM calls grow with corpus size [[r18]]. GraphRAG and RAPTOR are research code, so budget for engineering.

explain.title: Summaries mix documents
explain.md: A community summary draws on many source documents. If readers hold different permissions, a shared summary can leak facts from documents a reader may not see. This is a reasoned limit, not a quoted one: build summaries per permission scope or avoid the pattern.

whereToUse: Sensemaking over a stable corpus of reports, interviews, tickets or filings
Investigations that follow entities and relationships across many documents
Executive summaries of themes, trends and outliers
Corpora where local lookups already work and global questions are the gap

use: A meaningful share of questions are global or thematic
The corpus is entity-dense and relatively stable
You can pay for indexing or accept a deferred-cost variant
Source tracing is possible through the graph
avoid: Most questions are single-fact lookups that hybrid search answers
The corpus changes daily, forcing rebuilds
Permissions differ per reader inside the corpus
flips: Indexing budget is tight: test LazyGraphRAG-style deferral, noting the vendor numbers
Corpus updates frequently: prefer hybrid retrieval and an agentic planner
Only structure across levels is needed: consider a RAPTOR-style summary tree

pitfalls.symptom: Indexing cost explodes on a large corpus
pitfalls.cause: The standard method uses LLM calls for all graph steps
pitfalls.fix: Estimate on a sample, consider `FastGraphRAG` or a deferred-cost approach, and cap the corpus scope

pitfalls.symptom: Answers feel generic and cannot be traced to text
pitfalls.cause: Global answers come from community summaries, not source passages
pitfalls.fix: Expose the community and its source text units, and use Local mode for detail questions
Batch updates on a schedule or limit the graph to the stable part of the corpus

scenarios.title: Themes across five thousand incident reports
scenarios.situation: Analysts need recurring root causes, affected components and trends across five thousand closed incident reports. The archive grows monthly. Lookups of single incidents already work with hybrid search.
constraints: Moderate indexing budget, all analysts see all reports
unknowns: How many global questions per month?
Can analysts verify answers against sources?
scenarios.question: What do you add?

options.name: Pilot a graph-style index (LazyGraphRAG-style deferral or GraphRAG on a subset) beside the hybrid index and route global questions to it
options.why: Global questions are the documented gap of top-k retrieval [[r16]], and the archive is stable with shared access.
options.tradeoff: Extra indexing, a routing decision and vendor-reported cost numbers you must verify on your data.

options.name: Increase k and let the model summarise 200 chunks
options.why: Top-k chunks cover a sliver of the corpus and flood the context.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable for questions confined to one topic.

options.name: Replace hybrid with GraphRAG entirely
options.tradeoff: Lookups become costlier and slower than they need to be.

flips.then: Keep hybrid retrieval, and compute themes on a scheduled batch.

flips.if: Almost every question is a single-incident lookup
flips.then: Skip the graph index entirely and keep hybrid retrieval, since indexing cost buys nothing.

scenarios.takeaway: Route global questions to a global index.

scenarios.title: Per-department confidential reports
scenarios.situation: Reports are visible by department only. A leader asks 'what themes appear across all departments'.
unknowns: Is a cross-department view allowed at all?
scenarios.question: How do you answer thematic questions?

options.name: Build summaries per permission scope and aggregate only what the asker is entitled to see, or refuse cross-scope aggregation
options.why: A shared community summary mixes sources and can leak across permissions.
options.tradeoff: More indexes and weaker global views.

options.name: One global community summary set for everyone
options.why: Summaries embed facts from documents some readers cannot see.
options.tradeoff: Fine when every reader may see every document.

flips.if: Leadership is allowed to see everything
flips.then: A single graph index for that role is acceptable.

flips.if: Only anonymised, count-level themes are needed across departments
flips.then: Compute them from a metadata-only index that carries no document text, so no restricted content crosses a permission scope.

quiz.q: Which question is GraphRAG built for, and top-k vector RAG handles poorly?
options: What is the refund window in policy 12?
What are the main themes across all reports?
quiz.explain: Global, whole-corpus questions have no single nearest chunk. The others are local lookups that hybrid search handles [[r16]].

quiz.q: Match each method to its description.

pairs.r: Entities and relationships, Leiden communities, community summaries
Defers LLM work to query time, vendor-reported low cost
Recursive cluster and summarise tree of chunks
Indexing method that swaps some LLM steps for classic NLP

quiz.explain: These match the sources: GraphRAG docs, the Microsoft Research LazyGraphRAG blog and the RAPTOR paper.

quiz.q: The corpus changes daily and most questions are single-fact lookups. What do you choose?
quiz.explain: Daily changes make graph and tree rebuilds costly, and lookups do not need them. Hybrid retrieval with a reranker fits.

flashcards.front: What does GraphRAG add that top-k RAG lacks?
flashcards.back: A graph of entities and relationships with hierarchical community summaries, which lets it answer global questions.

flashcards.front: What cost numbers did Microsoft report for LazyGraphRAG (2024-11-25)?
flashcards.back: Indexing like vector RAG and 0.1% of GraphRAG, over 700 times lower query cost for comparable global quality. Vendor benchmark.

flashcards.front: Why can community summaries leak data?
flashcards.back: They blend facts from many documents, so readers with different permissions can see information they should not.
